headline: Karur Vysya Bank raises one-year MCLR to 9.30% effective November 22
hook: Loan costs inch higher for borrowers

modes.bear: Increased borrowing costs can weigh on loan growth and strain retail borrowers' repayment capacity.
modes.bull: Higher lending rates can protect the bank's net interest margins as funding costs fluctuate.
modes.simple: Karur Vysya Bank is raising its lending benchmark by a small margin, which means certain loans tied to this rate will become slightly more expensive.

summary: Karur Vysya Bank has announced an increase in its Marginal Cost of Funds-based Lending Rate (MCLR) by 5 basis points across all five tenures, with the benchmark one-year rate moving to 9.30%. At the same time, the bank is reducing its Base Rate and Benchmark Prime Lending Rate (BPLR) by 25 basis points starting November 22. The net impact on existing and new borrowers will vary depending on their specific loan benchmark, reset date, and applicable spread. Indian retail borrowers linked to the bank's MCLR will face higher monthly EMI outflows once their loan reset dates arrive.
why_it_matters: Higher MCLR means increased loan EMI outflows for borrowers.
winners_losers: Bank net interest margins gain / borrowers hurt

summary: Karur Vysya Bank received an interim stay from the Madras High Court regarding a show cause notice issued by the State Tax Officer.
